topicName: Native Build Systems: Gradle (Android) and CocoaPods / Xcode (iOS)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Native Build Systems: Gradle (Android) and CocoaPods / Xcode (iOS) in React Native"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"React Native bridges JavaScript development with native mobile platforms. While your core business logic lives in JavaScript, your app ultimately compiles into native binaries using Gradle for Android and CocoaPods/Xcode for iOS. Understanding these underlying build systems is essential for debugging native build failures, configuring dependencies, and scaling your React Native application."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Android Build System: Gradle and the Android folder"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Android applications in React Native are built using Gradle, an advanced build toolkit. The android directory in your project root contains all the native Android configurations."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"build.gradle (Project Level): Defines repositories and dependencies shared across all modules, such as the Android Gradle Plugin (AGP) version."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"build.gradle (Module Level - app): Controls app-specific configurations like application ID, min/target SDK versions, signing configs, and dependencies."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"settings.gradle: Defines which modules are included in the build, including autolinked React Native packages."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"// Example of adding a dependency in android/app/build.gradle
dependencies {
    implementation("com.facebook.react:react-android")
}"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"2. iOS Build System: CocoaPods and Xcode"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"iOS development revolves around Xcode and CocoaPods, the dependency manager for Swift and Objective-C Cocoa projects. In a React Native project, the ios directory houses your Xcode workspace (.xcworkspace) and the Podfile."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Podfile: Specifies external third-party native libraries and React Native sub-specs required for your iOS build."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":".xcworkspace: The primary workspace file you must open in Xcode, which encapsulates your project and its Pod dependencies."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"# Example Podfile configuration snippet in ios/Podfile
target 'MyApp' do
  config = use_native_modules!
  use_react_native!(
    :path => config[:reactNativePath]
  )
end"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Handling Native Dependencies and Autolinking"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"React Native features CLI autolinking, which automatically connects native Android and iOS modules to your build systems without manual linking steps. When you install a library like react-native-safe-area-context, the React Native CLI injects it into settings.gradle for Android and runs pod install for iOS."},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Troubleshooting Common Build Errors"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Build failures often stem from cache corruption or mismatched native dependencies. Clean your builds using the following standard commands when facing compilation issues:"},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"# Clean Android build
cd android && ./gradlew clean

# Reinstall and clean iOS pods
cd ios && pod deintegrate && pod install"}]
